mkdir -p /work/.github/workflows && cat > /work/.github/workflows/build.yml <<'EOF'
name: Java CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Change these to pick the JDK used for the build.
  # Supported distributions: temurin, zulu, corretto, liberica, microsoft,
  # oracle, semeru, sapmachine, graalvm, dragonwell, jetbrains, adopt-openj9.
  JAVA_DISTRIBUTION: temurin
  JAVA_VERSION: '21'

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Check out code
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Set up JDK ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }} (${{ env.JAVA_DISTRIBUTION }})
        uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        with:
          distribution: ${{ env.JAVA_DISTRIBUTION }}
          java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
          cache: ${{ hashFiles('pom.xml') != '' && 'maven' || 'gradle' }}

      - name: Show Java version
        run: java -version

      - name: Build with Maven
        if: hashFiles('pom.xml') != ''
        run: |
          if [ -f mvnw ]; then chmod +x mvnw && ./mvnw -B verify; else mvn -B verify; fi

      - name: Set up Gradle
        if: hashFiles('pom.xml') == '' && (hashFiles('build.gradle') != '' || hashFiles('build.gradle.kts') != '')
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4

      - name: Build with Gradle
        if: hashFiles('pom.xml') == '' && (hashFiles('build.gradle') != '' || hashFiles('build.gradle.kts') != '')
        run: |
          if [ -f gradlew ]; then chmod +x gradlew && ./gradlew build; else gradle build; fi
EOF

content.text:
I added the workflow at `.github/workflows/build.yml`. The YAML parses cleanly, but it hasn't been run on GitHub yet, since the repo has no Java code and no remote.

**Choosing the JDK:** the distribution and version are set in two variables at the top of the file:
```yaml
env:
  JAVA_DISTRIBUTION: temurin
  JAVA_VERSION: '21'
```
You can change them to any distribution `actions/setup-java` supports, such as `zulu`, `corretto`, `liberica`, `microsoft`, `oracle`, `semeru` or `graalvm`. The version can be a major version (`17`), an exact one (`21.0.4`) or a range.

**What it does:**
1. It runs on pushes to `main`/`master`, on pull requests, and when started manually. It only has read access to the repo contents.
2. It checks out the code and installs the chosen JDK with `actions/setup-java@v5`, then prints `java -version` so you can confirm which JDK was used.
3. It builds the project:
   - **Maven:** if there's a `pom.xml`, it runs `./mvnw -B verify`, or `mvn` if there's no wrapper. Maven dependencies are cached.
   - **Gradle:** if there's a `build.gradle(.kts)`, it uses `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4`, which handles caching, and runs `./gradlew build`, or `gradle` if there's no wrapper.

Because the repo is currently empty, every build step would be skipped until you add a `pom.xml` or Gradle build file. If you already know which build tool you'll use, I can remove the other branch to keep the file simpler. I haven't committed anything.
